issues.failure_explanation: The proof writes ‖γ(s)−(X+sV)‖² as a sum of squared norms of the individual Taylor terms. This requires all terms to be mutually orthogonal, which is false: for the same index set J (|J|≥2) the C-term s^{|J|+1} C×_{k∈J}[U̇_k 0]×_{k∉J}S_k and the G-term s^{|J|} G×_{k∈J}U̇_k×_{k∉J}U_k lie in the same subspace ⊗_{k∈J}span(U̇_k)⊗⊗_{k∉J}span(S_k) (e.g. for d=2, rank one: σu̇v̇ᵀ and C u̇v̇ᵀ are parallel), so cross terms appear. Moreover the next inequality bounds the order-s^4 contribution (d C-terms plus C(d,2) G-terms) by only C(d,1)=d terms, so the counting is unjustified. Hence the constant c(X)=(1/σ_min(X)²+1)^{d/2} is not established by the argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound ‖γ(s)−(X+sV)‖ by the triangle inequality over all Taylor terms using ‖U̇_k‖₂≤‖V‖/σ_min(X) and s‖V‖≤1; this yields a (possibly larger) explicit constant depending only on σ_min(X) and d, and the downstream constants are updated accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constant c(X) in (eq: curvature), and hence the explicit forms of ã and ā in Proposition prop: backtracking GRAP and the proof of prop: GRAP-R decrease, are unverified. The qualitative use (some continuous function of σ_min(X) bounding the projection error by s²‖V‖²) is unaffected.
issues.title: Curvature bound proof assumes orthogonality of non-orthogonal Taylor terms and miscounts them
issues.why_classification: A short standard estimate repairs the lemma with a different explicit constant; all downstream results only need a constant of this qualitative form, so no claim or rate is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\|\tensV_{\tensX_{\underline{\vecr}}}\|_\frob\neq 0$ (or the algorithm terminates otherwise), there exists (at least) one non-negative term.

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 3 the decrease δ(X̲) is proportional to δ̄(X̲), a minimum of two quantities evaluated at X̲. Non-stationarity of X̲ (by the paper's own normal-cone characterization) only requires that ∇f(X̲)×_{k∉I}P_{U̲_k}≠0 OR some k∉I term P^⊥_{U̲_k}(∇f)_{(k)}V_kG_{(k)}ᵀ≠0; it does not force both entries of the min to be nonzero. For example, ∇f(X̲)=a_k⊗(⊗_{j≠k}u̲_j) with a_k⊥u̲_k, k∉I, gives ∇f(X̲)×_{k∉I}P_{U̲}=0 while V_{X̲}≠0, so δ̄(X̲)=0 and δ(X̲)=0. The case split in the proof is on the point X_{r̲} (which depends on X), but the final lower bound ‖V_{X_{r̲}}‖²≥δ̄(X̲) is in terms of X̲ and degenerates to 0, so no strict decrease is proved for such X̲.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace δ̄(X̲) by ½(c_I‖∇f(X̲)×_{k∉I}P_{U̲_k}‖² + Σ_{k∉I}‖P^⊥_{U̲_k}(∇f(X̲))_{(k)}P_{Span(X̲_{(k)}ᵀ)}‖²), show via ‖V‖≥‖Ṽ‖ and the angle-condition decomposition that ‖V_{X_{r̲}}‖² dominates the corresponding quantity at X_{r̲}, use continuity of these projectors on the fixed-rank stratum, and use Proposition prop:added-1 to show the new quantity is positive at every non-stationary X̲.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficient decrease condition (and thus the contradiction argument in Theorem thm: GRAP-R) is not established for accumulation points in M_{≤r}∖(M_r∪M_{<r}) at which ∇f(X̲)⊥V_1⊗…⊗V_d or all row-space projections vanish but stationarity fails; apocalypse-freeness of GRAP-R is unproved in that regime.
issues.title: Case 3 sufficient-decrease constant δ̄(X̲) can be zero at non-stationary mixed-rank points
issues.why_classification: The result is recoverable with the paper's own tools, but it requires re-deriving the lower bound with a different quantity and a positivity argument via the normal-cone characterization, i.e. a contained non-trivial fix rather than a local edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $\underline{\matx}\neq 0$, it holds that $\underline{r}\leq \rank(\matx)$ for all $\matx\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $\|\matx-\underline{\matx}\|_\frob<\sigma_{\min}(\underline{\matx})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lower bounds r̲_k≤rank(X_{(k)}) and rank(X_{(k)})=r_k for k∉I are attributed to Proposition prop: rank delta, whose hypothesis is ‖X−X̲‖<σ_min(X̲). Unlike Cases 2–3 of prop: GRAP-R decrease, the radius ε(X̲) here contains no σ_min(X̲) term, so the hypothesis is not ensured. Without it, r̆ (with r̆_k=r_k for k∉I) need not lie in I_1×…×I_d and X̲ need not lie in M_{≤r̆}, so the subsequent use of Lemma lem: HOSVD inequality to get ‖X_{r̆}−X̲‖≤(√d+1)‖X−X̲‖ is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: \rank_\Delta(\matx_{(k)})\leq\underline{r}_k\leq\rank(\matx_{(k)})$ for all $k\in I$ and $\rank(\matx_{(k)})=r_k=\underline{r}_k$ for $k\in[d]\setminus I$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the term σ_min(X̲)/(2(√d+1)) to ε(X̲) (when X̲≠0), exactly as in the GRAP-R proof, so that Proposition prop: rank delta applies to every mode.
issues.overall_effect: The existence and closeness of the lower-rank candidate X_{r̆} in Case 2 of prop: rfGRAP are not justified as written.
issues.title: Neighborhood radius in rfGRAP-R proof omits the σ_min condition needed to invoke Proposition prop: rank delta
issues.why_classification: A one-term local adjustment of the radius, already used elsewhere in the paper, restores the argument with no loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider $\breve{\vecr}=(\breve{r}_1,\breve{r}_2,\dots,\breve{r}_d)$ with $\breve{r}_k=\min\{r_k-1,\rank(\matx_{(k)})\}$ for $k\in I$ and $\breve{r}_k=r_k$ for $k\in[d]\setminus I$.
Similar to case 3 in the proof of~\cref{prop: GRAP-R decrease}, the analysis above does not depend on a specific choice of Tucker decompositions

issues.failure_explanation: The rank-decreasing mechanism of Algorithm alg: rfGRAP-R drops at most one rank per mode, so the candidate X_{r̆} has Tucker rank r̆ with r̆_k=min{r_k−1,rank(X_{(k)})}, which can exceed r̲_k=rank_k(X̲) (e.g. X=X̲ plus a small rank-2 perturbation in mode k∈I with r_k≥r̲_k+2). Then X_{r̆} and X̲ lie in different strata, and for k∈I the projectors P_{Ŭ_k}, P^⊥_{Ŭ_k}, P_{Span(X_{r̆,(k)}ᵀ)} do not converge to their counterparts at X̲ (different dimensions), so the claimed bound ‖P̃_k(∇f(X_{r̆}))‖≥½‖P̃_k(∇f(X̲))‖ 'for all k∈[d]' on a neighbourhood is unjustified. The final inequality ‖V_{X_r̆}‖≥(√c_I/2)Π(1/min)^{1/2}‖V̂_{X̲}‖ relies on these k∈I terms, so the lower bound on the decrease in terms of X̲ is not established. (The constant c_I is also evaluated with r̲ although the candidate has rank r̆, and the stated products over k of c_I/min² are inconsistent, but these only affect positive constants.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain only the stratum-independent quantities: use ‖V_{X_r̆}‖²≥‖V̂_{X_r̆}‖²≥(1/(d+1))[Π_{k∈I}(1/min{n_k,n_{-k}})‖∇f(X_{r̆})×_{k∉I}P_{Ŭ_k}‖² + Σ_{k∉I}‖P^⊥_{Ŭ_k}(∇f(X_{r̆}))_{(k)}P_{Span(X_{r̆,(k)}ᵀ)}‖²], note that for k∉I both X_{r̆} and X̲ have full mode-k rank r_k so these projectors are continuous, and use Proposition prop:added-1 to show the corresponding quantity at X̲ is positive whenever X̲ is non-stationary; define δ(X̲) from it.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficient decrease condition for rfGRAP-R, and hence the apocalypse-freeness claim of Theorem thm:added-1, is unproved for non-stationary accumulation points X̲ in a rank-deficient stratum when nearby iterates have rank exceeding rank(X̲)+1 in some deficient mode.
issues.title: rfGRAP-R lower bound on ‖V_{X_r̆}‖ uses continuity across different rank strata (r̆ ≠ rank(X̲))
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is recoverable without new architecture, but requires replacing the lower-bound argument by a contained new derivation (dropping the k∈I terms and invoking the normal-cone characterization) rather than a local edit.
